_about: Language-agnostic spec for a deterministic cost-tier router. THIS FILE is the reusable asset: any app (Go/Rust/TS/Python/bash) loads it and implements the matcher — lowercase the task, select a tier per `strategy`, then apply length_rules → bias → cache → escalation → budget → latency → clamps. See README.md. route.sh is the reference implementation; bench.sh scores any implementation against evalset.tsv (and `--cache` against cache-evalset.tsv).
_strategy_note: first-match (walk rules in order, first match wins) | max-hits (tier with most matching rules wins) | weighted (sum of rule.weight per tier). Default first-match keeps parity with compass-route.sh.
_bias_note: cheap | balanced | quality. On a LOW-confidence pick only: cheap downgrades one tier, quality upgrades one — never past clamps. balanced = no change.

haiku.use: mechanical / low-reasoning: typos, renames, formatting, comments, version bumps, one-liners

sonnet.use: default: features, fixes, tests, refactors, docs

opus.use: high-stakes reasoning: architecture, security/auth/crypto, concurrency, migrations, multi-tenancy, protocol/threat design

_cost_note: cost is a RELATIVE weight (~output $/Mtok ratio: haiku 1 : sonnet 4 : opus 20). `latency` is a RELATIVE speed weight (lower = faster). Override per app via `profiles`.
_budget_note: Spend governor (stage, OFF unless COMPASS_ROUTE_BUDGET_USD is set). spent = COMPASS_ROUTE_SPENT_USD or sum of today's ${COMPASS_HOME}/spend.tsv. At warn_pct of budget it cheap-biases LOW-confidence picks; at cap_pct it applies cap_ceiling as a hard cost cap (don't burn opus when nearly out). A deliberate operator dial — opt-in.
_profiles_note: select with --profile NAME; a profile overrides per-tier cost/model. Use it so bench.sh savings reflect YOUR prices and so each app (lantern/kage) maps tiers to its own models.
_clamps_note: hard bounds applied LAST. floor = never route below; ceiling = never above (cost cap). allow = explicit allowlist (overrides floor/ceiling when non-empty). Override per run: --floor/--ceiling/--allow.
_cache_note: Cache-aware cost-min (stage 4.5, OFF unless COMPASS_ROUTE_WARM names already-warm tier(s)). Among tiers in [pick..ceiling] it rides a WARM pricier tier when its EXPECTED cost is lower than the cold pick: cost = (warm? read_mult : write_mult)*tier.cost*P + tier.cost*D + tier.cost*out_weight*O, reusing each tier's relative `cost`. Models Anthropic prompt-cache economics (read 0.1x; 5m write 1.25x / 1h write_mult_long 2x). UPGRADE-ONLY — never routes below the pick, so quality can't drop; clamps still bound it. P/D/O default here, overridable via COMPASS_PREFIX_TOKENS / COMPASS_TASK_TOKENS / COMPASS_OUTPUT_TOKENS; TTL via COMPASS_ROUTE_TTL=5m|1h (recommend with --ttl from COMPASS_ROUTE_REUSES / COMPASS_ROUTE_GAP_MIN). See docs/adr/0004-cache-aware-routing.md.
_classifier_note: OFF by default. A local Naive-Bayes tier classifier (train-classifier.sh from --log judgments) used as a free/fast fallback layer before the LLM. Toggle on with ROUTER_CLASSIFIER=on or enabled:true once you've logged enough data. classify.sh ABSTAINS when off / no model / margin<min_margin, so fallback-cascade.sh falls through to the LLM judge. The progression: heuristic -> classifier -> LLM, paid for by data the LLM judge already labeled.
_escalation_note: if the pick's confidence < threshold (0 = off): when `fallback` is set it is run (the task is piped on stdin; it prints a tier) and that tier is used — the cascade: heuristic for the confident majority, a smarter call (LLM/classifier) for the ambiguous middle. With no fallback, the tier is bumped one step. Override: --escalate-below N, --fallback CMD.
_length_note: raise the floor for long tasks: a task with >= min_words is forced to at least `at_least` (a 60-word 'comment …' task isn't really trivial). Applied before bias/escalation.
_rules_note: ordered. Each: tier, pattern (ERE, matched case-insensitively), reason, optional `weight` (max-hits/weighted strategies), optional `unless` (ERE that VETOES this rule when it also matches — e.g. opus 'unless' a trivial qualifier).
_domains_note: optional SECOND axis (orthogonal to tier): --domain also emits a specialist (ui/api/infra/docs/core) via first-match, for apps that dispatch to domain agents. 'core' is the catch-all.
